rust_side.symbol: A* search loop (per reports/capability-validation/algorithms/001-a_star.md, lines 231-295): open_set of candidate DFGs scored by a HAND-DESIGNED heuristic combining coverage (weight 0.8), simplicity/density (weight 0.2), and an edge-count penalty (weight 0.2) -- NOT a distance-to-goal heuristic over a well-defined state-space metric.
rust_side.admissibility_assessment: Classical A* optimality (Hart/Nilsson/Raphael 1968) requires an admissible heuristic (never overestimates true remaining cost) over a well-defined cost function. This Rust heuristic is a composite quality SCORE for candidate models, not a lower-bound estimate of remaining search cost to an optimality target -- there is no 'true cost' function it could be checked against for admissibility. The search is a bounded beam search (open_set truncated to 128 candidates each iteration, fast_discovery.rs) dressed in A* terminology, not textbook A* over a metric space.
rust_side.conclusion: Even if mfact/mfw had a general A*-admissibility theorem (a broader search than done here found none), it could not be invoked for this specific implementation -- the admissibility precondition is not just unformalized, it does not clearly apply to this heuristic's design at all.

lean_carrier.theorem: hasL1Loop_iff: hasL1Loop l = true <-> exists i, i + 1 < l.length and idx l i = idx l (i+1)
lean_carrier.definitions: hasL1Loop, hasL2Loop, hasRework (Bool-valued, structural recursion on List Nat), idx (zero-default indexing via headD/drop, avoiding List.get! which is not in core Lean's Init)
lean_carrier.no_mathlib: Deliberately imports nothing -- mfact's procint/.lake package cache has zero Mathlib build artifacts (confirmed: `ls .lake/packages/mathlib/.lake/build` fails), so a `lake build` from this state would require a full from-scratch Mathlib build, impractical to run inline. Verified instead with a direct `lean` invocation of the pinned toolchain (leanprover/lean4:v4.31.0) on the standalone file: exit 0, zero warnings, zero errors.
lean_carrier.axiom_check: #print axioms ProcInt.MFW.hasL1Loop_iff -> [propext, Quot.sound] only -- the two standard trusted kernel axioms essentially every nontrivial Lean proof depends on. No sorry, no custom axiom declared anywhere in the file.
